cb_step_1.title: Select the spine CT scan
cb_step_1.simple: Select the CT volume you want to use for planning.
cb_step_1.detailed: This CT is the foundation of the entire plan: every landmark, trajectory, and screw measurement will be taken from it. Choose the scan that best shows the spinal levels you intend to treat, making sure the anatomy of interest is inside the scan range.

cb_step_2.title: Continue from image loading
cb_step_2.simple: Click Next to proceed from the image-loading page.
cb_step_2.detailed: This confirms that the selected CT is loaded and moves you to the next planning stage. If you notice the wrong scan or an incomplete field of view, go back and select a different volume before continuing.

cb_step_3.title: Get a clear view of the treatment region
cb_step_3.simple: Rotate, zoom, and pan the views so the spinal region you are about to define is clearly visible.
cb_step_3.detailed: This step only reorients the view so you can see the surgical region of interest comfortably before defining it. Take your time to center the relevant vertebrae and choose the vantage that will let you recognize the anatomy in the following steps. No marking or clicking is needed here.

cb_step_4.title: Choose the instrumentation plan
cb_step_4.simple: Select the vertebral levels to instrument, the number of sides, and the approach direction.
cb_step_4.detailed: These choices define the scope of the whole plan: which levels will receive screws, whether the construct is on one or both sides, and the surgical approach direction, for example posterior trajectories. The rest of the workflow will generate landmarks, trajectories, and screws only for the levels and sides you specify, so verify this matches the intended construct before continuing.

cb_step_5.title: Confirm the surgical region of interest
cb_step_5.simple: Click Next to continue from the surgical region of interest page.
cb_step_5.detailed: This finalizes the region you reviewed and allows the workflow to use it as the working volume for all subsequent landmark and screw computations. The next steps will orient the slices and place landmarks within this region.

cb_step_6.title: Turn on slice intersection controls
cb_step_6.simple: Turn on slice intersection visibility, enable Set interaction, and switch on both Translate and Rotate.
cb_step_6.detailed: These toolbar controls let you move and rotate the slice-plane intersections directly in the 3D view. This is needed in the next step to align the viewing planes with the orientation of the spine before you place any landmark points.

cb_step_7.title: Align the red slice to the spine
cb_step_7.simple: Rotate and pan the red slice view so the spine segment you are working on is clearly visible in the orientation you need.
cb_step_7.detailed: Here you only reorient the view — rotate, zoom, and pan, using the slice intersection controls if needed — to get the best vantage of the vertebrae for landmark placement. A well-aligned slice makes the point placement that follows faster and more anatomically accurate.

cb_step_8.title: Start placing landmark points
cb_step_8.simple: Click the 'Place a control point' button to start placing points.
cb_step_8.detailed: This activates point placement so the clicks you make in the 2D views are recorded as landmark points for the current spine part. You will mark one spinal part per pass, then stop placement before moving on.

cb_step_9.title: Mark the points for one spine part
cb_step_9.simple: In the 2D views, click on the part of the spine you are working on to record its landmark points.
cb_step_9.detailed: Click on the anatomical points that define one part of the spine — for example one vertebral level or one side of the construct — so the tool can build the reference for screw trajectory planning from them. Mark one part per pass, choosing clinically relevant landmarks that are clearly visible on the CT. When the part is fully marked, finish that pass before starting the next part.

cb_step_10.title: Stop point placement
cb_step_10.simple: Click the 'Place a control point' button again to switch off point placement.
cb_step_10.detailed: This ends the current point-placing pass and keeps the points you just recorded for this spine part. You can then decide whether another part still needs to be marked.

cb_step_11.title: Check that all parts are marked
cb_step_11.simple: Choose Yes if every spine part now has its points; choose No to go back and mark the next part.
cb_step_11.detailed: This step asks whether all required spine parts have been marked with landmark points. If parts remain, you will return to view adjustment and point placement for the next part; once all parts are done, the workflow locks in the point set and continues.

cb_step_12.title: Lock the slice intersections
cb_step_12.simple: In the slice intersection interaction options, turn off Set interaction.
cb_step_12.detailed: With the landmark points now correctly placed, this disables further movement of the slice-plane intersections so the views can no longer be shifted accidentally while you work with the landmarks.

cb_step_13.title: Select level, side, and landmarks
cb_step_13.simple: Using the selection widget, set the level, side, and landmarks that should be used for the planned points.
cb_step_13.detailed: For each instrumented level, tell the workflow which side and which anatomical landmarks define the expected point set. This ties the previously placed points to the correct vertebra and side, which is essential for computing meaningful screw trajectories and measurements.

cb_step_14.title: Continue after landmark placement
cb_step_14.simple: Click Next to continue from the landmark placement page.
cb_step_14.detailed: This confirms that the landmark points are correctly assigned and moves you to the puncture-site and screw part of the plan. From here, each trajectory will be defined using the landmarks you just set.

cb_step_15.title: Choose the puncture site and screw diameter
cb_step_15.simple: Choose the puncture site and the screw diameter (in mm) for the current trajectory.
cb_step_15.detailed: The puncture site is the intended skin entry point for the trajectory, and the screw diameter must be matched to the pedicle dimensions at the instrumented level. These settings directly define the planned screw geometry that will later be evaluated. Configure one puncture site per pass, then confirm it before moving to the next.

cb_step_16.title: Adjust the view of the puncture site
cb_step_16.simple: Rotate, zoom, and pan the 2D views so the start and end of the puncture site are clearly visible.
cb_step_16.detailed: This step only reorients the 2D views so you can see the entry and target points of the puncture site clearly before positioning them. A good vantage helps you set the start and end of the puncture trajectory accurately in the steps that follow.

cb_step_17.title: Update the plan
cb_step_17.simple: Click Update to refresh the planned trajectory with your current settings.
cb_step_17.detailed: This recomputes the trajectory and its measurements from the chosen puncture site and screw size, so you can check that the updated geometry looks correct before accepting it.

cb_step_18.title: Confirm the puncture site
cb_step_18.simple: Click OK to accept the configured puncture site.
cb_step_18.detailed: This accepts the start and end positions and the chosen screw size for this puncture site and saves it into the plan. After confirming, you can proceed to configure the next puncture site if the plan requires it.

cb_step_19.title: Check that all puncture sites are configured
cb_step_19.simple: Choose Yes if every puncture site has been configured; choose No to configure the next site.
cb_step_19.detailed: This step confirms that all planned puncture sites have been set and accepted. If any site is still missing, you will return to the puncture-site selection to complete it; otherwise the workflow moves on to screw adjustment and grading.

cb_step_20.title: Continue to screw adjustment
cb_step_20.simple: Click Next to continue from the screw adjustment page.
cb_step_20.detailed: This moves the workflow to the stage where the planned screws are reviewed and can be further adjusted before they are graded.

cb_step_21.title: Grade the planned screws
cb_step_21.simple: Click Grade Screws to generate the table that rates each planned screw.
cb_step_21.detailed: The workflow evaluates every planned screw against the bony anatomy — for example checking how well it fits within the pedicle and how safely it clears critical structures — and produces a grading table. This lets you identify which trajectories are acceptable and which may need revision.

cb_step_22.title: Review the screw grades
cb_step_22.simple: Review the grading table for all planned screws.
cb_step_22.detailed: Go through the grade of each planned screw. Pay particular attention to screws with poor grades, as these may indicate trajectories that need to be revised for safety. If a screw is graded poorly, adjust the corresponding puncture site or screw settings and re-run the grading before finalizing the plan.

cb_step_23.title: Finish the grading step
cb_step_23.simple: Click Next to continue past the grading page.
cb_step_23.detailed: This completes the screw-grading review and continues the workflow toward finalizing the surgical plan. Once this step is finished, the planned trajectory and screw construct are ready for the next phase of the procedure.
